text:
marta: Heads-up: deploying websvc 1.14.0 to prod at 23:00 PT tonight. Doing a constrained rollout (5% canary for 15m) + smoke. Need a quick runbook sanity check & rollback ack. Ping owners: @kevin @jamal

ops-bot: Scheduled deploy created: websvc-1.14.0 -> prod window 23:00-23:30 PT. CI checks: all green.

kevin: I'll push and monitor. Can someone confirm who flips the feature flag if we need a fast rollback?

jamal: I can flip the ff. Flag name: ff_websvc_v2. Quick rollback trigger thresholds I suggest: >0.8% 5xx error rate OR 30% increase in p95 latency vs baseline sustained for >3m.

olga: Runbook (condensed) — paste for quick ops:
1) Disable canary routing: `curl -X POST "https://ops.internal/api/routes/canary" -d '{"service":"websvc","enabled":false}'`
2) Promote previous release: `infra roll promote websvc@1.13.7`
3) If sessions stale, clear cache on web tier: `redis-cli -h redis-prod flushdb` (use with care)
4) Verify health: `/health` should be 200 across all nodes
Escalation: if rollback fails or errors spike further, page oncall and set incident channel.

marta: Smoke checklist to run after canary (I'll run these):
- curl /health 5x from us-west/us-east/eu
- run sample 50 user queries from staging promptset against canary
- check traces for any sudden 5xx or DB errors
- confirm error budget metrics on dashboard

kevin: Timeline plan: 23:00 start -> 23:00-23:15 canary -> decision 23:15-23:20 -> if green, full rollout 23:20-23:25. If canary unhealthy, rollback immediately per runbook.

jamal: Rollback command I'll execute if needed: `infra rollback websvc --to 1.13.7 --force` — I'll be on standby and ready to flip ff and run the rollback.

ops-bot: Reminder: runbook located at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/websvc-rollback (access: ops + eng). Full rollout requires 2 approvals.

marta: Ack from me :thumbsup: Please react with :eyes: when you're online for the window so we have confirmations.

kevin: :eyes: I'll be at my desk starting 22:50 PT and through 00:30.

olga: :eyes: standby and can help validate traces post-canary.
